do_not_assume: The Rock-side name becomes the App Store name.
Saving the Rock record packages or publishes an App Store application.
goal: A Rock-managed Apple TV application with a valid Start Screen and explicitly reviewed application settings.
steps: Confirm Rock 14 or later.
Open `Admin Tools > CMS Configuration > Apple TV Apps`.
Create the application with an internal name and optional description.
Review global styles, page-view tracking, retention, API key, and Authentication Page.
Save and open the generated Start Screen.
Add the smallest valid TVML document that the target shell can render.
Test the Start Screen in the target Apple TV client.
Identify the target platform.
Confirm the installed Rock version: Apple TV requires Rock 14 or later; Roku requires Rock 16.7 or later.
Confirm that the expected TV application administration blocks and site types exist in the installed package.
Confirm the operator has permission to view and administer the relevant CMS configuration pages.
For Roku development, verify whether the current Core-team development-application process is required and has been completed.
Stop page-level debugging until the application record can be opened. Apple TV Docs Roku Docs
title: Recipe: Create an Apple TV application skeleton

do_not_assume: Show in Menu creates navigation automatically.
HTML or TVML can be reused as SceneGraph.
Do not assume the Roku shell creates menus automatically from the setting.
goal: A Roku page whose rendered SceneGraph loads with deterministic initial focus.
steps: Confirm Rock 16.7 or later and an available Roku development shell.
Open the intended Roku application record and review its application settings.
Create a page with the required name and cache settings.
Render a `Rock:Page` as the outer component.
Add one focusable `Rock:Button` with a unique ID.
Set `initialFocus` to that ID.
Validate the post-Lava SceneGraph.
Load the page on the Roku client and test directional focus.
Confirm that the page setting is enabled.
Inspect the Lava that constructs the menu.
Confirm that the page collection and Show in Menu value are actually read by that Lava.
Confirm that the resulting SceneGraph contains an actionable menu item.
Do not assume the Roku shell creates menus automatically from the setting.
title: Recipe: Build a Roku content page

do_not_assume: Context survives after the application closes.
Public caching is safe for context-dependent output.
Two individually failing commands will work when chained.
goal: Selecting one control sets a context value and opens a destination page that reads it.
steps: Choose a context key and bounded value.
Confirm the destination page reads that key from `Context`.
Place `setContext` on a supported Rock control and test it independently.
Place `pushPage` on a supported control and test the destination independently.
Combine the commands with comma-separated names.
Keep the context and navigation parameters on the actionable control.
Test a fresh application session and a session where the context is changed.
Add `clearContext` to the appropriate reset path.
title: Recipe: Add Roku navigation with application context

do_not_assume: The application API key secures the website Remote Authentication page.
The website Authentication Page and TV login-display page are the same page.
A code from one device session can authenticate another.
goal: A person can authenticate on a website and the TV client transitions to the configured success page.
steps: Create an external website page containing the Remote Authentication block.
Associate the block with the intended TV application site.
Give the page a reachable route.
Select that website page as the application’s Authentication Page.
Create distinct TV pages for login display, timeout, and success.
Add the platform-specific QR-code and code placeholders or recognized Roku control IDs.
Add a `login` command with the three TV-page destinations.
Test QR navigation, manual-code entry, timeout, success, and Back behavior.
Test while signed out of the website and while already signed in.
Confirm the application record points to the intended external website Authentication Page.
Confirm that page contains the Remote Authentication block.
Confirm the block is associated with the correct TV application site.
Confirm the person can reach the website route.
For Apple TV, verify the login page contains the single-brace `{ authQrCodeUrl }` and `{ authCode }` placeholders.
For Roku, verify the page contains controls with IDs `lgnQrPoster` and `lgnCodeLabel`.
Confirm the login command targets the correct login, timeout, and success TV pages. Creating an Apple TV Sign-in Page
title: Recipe: Configure remote TV sign-in

do_not_assume: A YouTube URL can be passed to the media command.
A watch map alone appends to the original interaction.
goal: A supported media resource plays and resumes according to an explicitly selected interaction strategy.
steps: Choose a direct MP4 or HLS video URL, or a direct MP3 audio URL.
Prove playback with only the command and direct URL.
If the resource is a Rock Media Element, add its identifier.
Add title, subtitle, artwork, and description as needed.
Decide whether to resume from prior state or append to an existing interaction.
For resume-only, pass the prior watch map.
To append, pass both the prior interaction identifier and watch map.
Test first play, interrupted play, resumed play, and completion.
Confirm whether a new or existing interaction was expected.
title: Recipe: Add tracked media playback with resume

do_not_assume: HTML/CSS behavior transfers directly to TVML.
A page-specific theme fixes hard-coded colors.
Simulator appearance proves the final television presentation.
goal: One TVML page remains legible in both Light and Dark themes.
steps: Apply global application styles through the documented site-style mechanism.
Add Light and Dark `tv-template` media-query rules for colors that need to change.
Use documented TVML text styles before introducing custom font choices.
Test the page in both user-selected themes.
If declaring a page-specific theme, retest all text, imagery, badges, and focus states.
Validate shadows and overlays for clipping.
title: Recipe: Make an Apple TV page theme-aware
